sections.label: Employment Security Fund contributions and payouts
sections.summary: Employees and employers each pay 0.05% of monthly salary into an Employment Security Fund, giving redundant workers 40% of last drawn salary for up to six months.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thus, the important thing is to pool the uneven risk that is being felt across generations of workers in an equitable and progressive manner.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We propose that employees pay 0.05% of their monthly salary into an Employment Security Fund, which would be matched by employers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Based on the average wage, excluding Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions in 2014, the proposed 0.1% would amount to an average monthly contribution of $3.80 per worker.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If a worker is made redundant, he or she will receive a payout of 40% of his or her last drawn salary for up to six months.

sections.label: Minimum payout for low-wage workers
sections.summary: The proposal sets a minimum payout of $500 a month to benefit low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We should also better protect our most vulnerable workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We propose that the minimum payout would be $500 a month so as to benefit low-wage workers.

sections.label: Redundancy levels in 2016 and 2017
sections.summary: Redundancies reached 19,170 in 2016, with 4,000-plus redundancies each quarter since late 2015 and an estimated 4,800 in the first quarter of 2017.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Redundancies reached 19,170 in 2016, the highest rate since the 2008/2009 global financial crisis.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2016, higher redundancies have become the new normal.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We have not seen peaks but a plateau of 4,000-plus redundancies each quarter since the fourth quarter of 2015.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The first quarter of 2017 of estimated 4,800 redundancies suggest that the new normal of constant, high redundancies will continue.

sections.label: Payouts for self-employed individuals
sections.summary: Self-employed individuals receive 40% of average last drawn income for the previous six months, subject to a median wage cap, capped at one series of payouts every three years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Self-employed individuals will receive a payout of 40% of their average last drawn income for the previous six months subject to the same median wage cap should they become unable to earn an income due to the involuntary winding up of their businesses or termination of contract for service, capped at one series of payouts every three years.

sections.label: Redundancy insurance payouts reduce financial strain
sections.summary: Payouts from redundancy insurance help workers stay focused on the task instead of being distracted by financial strain.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But for them to do so, they need to be focused on the task and not be distracted by the strain on their finances.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is where the payouts from redundancy insurance would help.

sections.label: Self-sustainable Employment Security Fund window closing
sections.summary: A properly calibrated and timely redundancy insurance scheme would make the Employment Security Fund self-sustainable and cost the Government close to nothing, but the window is closing fast.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Yet, another benefit of the redundancy insurance scheme is that when it is properly calibrated and launched in a timely manner, the Employment Security Fund would become self-sustainable in the long run and would cost the Government close to nothing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Given the Manpower Minister's ominous Labour Day warning that unemployment will rise in the near future as we go head long into economic restructuring amidst technological and social disruption, we believe the window of opportunity for implementing a redundancy insurance scheme is closing fast.

sections.label: Redundancy insurance in other countries
sections.summary: Redundancy insurance programmes in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and South Korea involve roughly equal employer and employee contributions with little public expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, redundancy insurance programmes in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and South Korea involve more or less equivalent contributions from employers and employees with little public expenditure.

sections.label: Redundancy insurance as safety net
sections.summary: Redundancy insurance is useful as a safety net for affected workers and also serves as a trampoline for reskilling and new careers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In such a situation, redundancy insurance is useful as a safety net for affected workers and, I must emphasise, also serves as a trampoline for workers to reskill and find new career directions.

sections.label: Targeted redundancy insurance scheme proposed
sections.summary: The proposed scheme is a targeted redundancy insurance scheme, not an unemployment insurance scheme, taking local situation, workforce culture and existing programmes into account.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The scheme proposed here is not any unemployment insurance scheme but a targeted redundancy insurance scheme that takes the local situation, workforce culture and existing Government programmes into account.

sections.label: Downside of automatic insurance payouts
sections.summary: The most serious downside with automatic insurance payouts is that it reduces the incentive to find work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The most serious downside with automatic insurance payouts is that it reduces the incentive to find work.

sections.label: Canada premium comparison
sections.summary: Using the Member's data, comparing countries with similar benefits, Canada's premium is 4.4%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Using data the Member provided, just comparing countries with similar benefits, Canada's premium is 4.4%.

sections.label: Realistic assumptions on scheme cost
sections.summary: With more realistic assumptions, the scheme is much more likely to cost at least 1% to 2% of wages, raising employer costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If we make more realistic assumptions, the scheme is much more likely to cost at least 1% to 2% of wages, and then we have to consider how it will raise costs for employers.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits and redundancy premiums
sections.summary: It asks whether employers will pay less retrenchment benefits after paying redundancy premiums, and concludes the present approach should continue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Will employers be less willing to pay workers retrenchment benefits, since they have already paid the premiums for the redundancy?

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Therefore, all things considered, we should persist with our present approach.

sections.label: Risks of getting it wrong
sections.summary: Getting it wrong could bring more long-term unemployment, more redundancy, lower retrenchment benefits, higher business costs and false worker security.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If we get it wrong, we could end up with more long-term unemployment, more redundancy, lower retrenchment benefits, higher cost burden to businesses and, worst of all, a false sense of security for the workers.

sections.label: Government employment support schemes
sections.summary: Schemes provide wage support, training subsidies and temporary relief, fully funded by the Government, with employment support emphasised against unemployment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have built up many schemes to help workers keep their jobs and help those who lose their jobs find new ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We provide generous wage support, training subsidies and temporary relief.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government provides full funding for these programmes without putting the burden on our businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To guard against unemployment, we emphasise employment support because it is still the best way forward.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits not replaced
sections.summary: The speaker says he never suggested replacing retrenchment benefits with redundancy insurance, and understands the risk of employers thinking premiums replace payouts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: In response to Mr Patrick Tay, in no way am I suggesting that retrenchment benefits should be replaced.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: And I did not mention that at all − that it should be replaced by redundancy insurance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: I understand that this is part of the cons of the redundancy insurance scheme − the risk that employers would have that kind of mentality and attitude, where they think, "Since I am paying the premiums, I do not have to pay out retrenchment benefits.

sections.label: Definition of redundancy
sections.summary: Redundancy is defined by jobs no longer being needed, following the Ministry of Manpower definition, and does not exclude the terminations mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Regarding the Member's second question about redundancy, our definition of redundancy is really based on if the jobs are no longer needed and people are being laid off because these jobs are no longer needed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: This follows the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) definition, and it does not exclude some of the terminations the Member was talking about, in terms of job fit and what not.
